as_told.title: ScanPyramids muon scanning funded by a Japanese team with the Ministry of Antiquities

plain: This story is about ScanPyramids, a project that began around 2015 to look for hidden empty spaces inside the pyramids of Giza in Egypt. A scientist named Filippo Biondi, who has worked on scanning beneath the pyramids, describes it on a podcast with the host Jesse Michels. He says the project uses muons, tiny particles that rain down on Earth from space and can pass through stone. A pyramid researcher named Geoffrey Drumm also talks about it on a later episode. He says a Japanese team has been paying for the work, alongside Egypt's Ministry of Antiquities, the government office in charge of ancient sites. He also points to the project's published paper on muons. If its findings hold, it would mean the pyramids still hold rooms or passages no one has entered.
